clue.text: Spurs letting in header from Newcastle? Nuts!

indicators.note: letting in means the spurs word admits another letter inside it

parts.note: to spur is to goad, so spurs gives goads

indicators.note: header from means the first letter of Newcastle is taken

explanation.surface: A football fan exclaims at Tottenham Hotspur letting in a headed goal against Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs and Newcastle look like football teams; one is a verb and the other just supplies N.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is slang for testicles, the male reproductive glands.

clue.text: Interrogators try to keep tapes running

indicators.note: to keep means the try word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: to have a go is to try, so try gives go

indicators.note: running means the letters of tapes are set going into a new order

explanation.surface: Interrogators attempt to keep the recorder tapes going during questioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' makes ESTAP from tapes, which sits between G and O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nazi secret police were notorious for brutal questioning of suspects.

clue.text: Lisping Scandinavian makes a point

indicators.note: lisping means the sibilant sound at the end of the Scandinavian word is spoken as th instead

parts.note: Norse means Scandinavian, of old Norway

explanation.surface: Someone from Scandinavia with a lisp manages to make a point in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: NORSE ends in an s sound; a lisp turns that s into th, giving the compass word.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the four cardinal compass points.

clue.text: Run through key prelude's opening parts

indicators.note: parts means that first letter splits the key word apart and sits inside it

parts.note: the delete key on a keyboard

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of prelude is taken

explanation.surface: A pianist runs through the key passages that open a prelude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks musical but is the computer's delete key; P goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete supplies is to use them up, exhausting them.

clue.text: Abstainer dropping special sort of acid

indicators.note: dropping means a letter falls out of the abstainer word

parts.note: an ascetic is someone who abstains from pleasures

explanation.surface: A teetotaller gives up a special kind of acid trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing S from ASCETIC leaves the acid of vinegar.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic acid is the compound that gives vinegar its sharpness.

clue.text: German author not beginning scary story

indicators.note: not beginning means the author's name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Friedrich Schiller was a German poet and dramatist

explanation.surface: A German writer who was never known for horror stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A thriller meant to send shivers down the spine is called this.

clue.text: A period when expecting to prune trees anew

parts.note: to prune a plant is to trim it

indicators.note: anew means the letters of trees are made over in a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener's advice on the season to cut back trees again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expecting' reads as anticipating, but here it means pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: Pregnancy is divided into three stages of about three months each.

clue.text: About time row gets more unpleasant

parts.note: CA, from circa, means about
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A quarrel over the hour makes things nastier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' tempts as a quarrel, but it is a row of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Catty means spiteful, so the comparative is spitefuller or nastier.

clue.text: Demon's dirty bomb disheartened country

indicators.note: disheartened means the hearts are removed, keeping only the outer letters of each word

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A terrorist's dirty bomb has demoralised a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' covers both dirty and bomb, stripping each to its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jewish folklore it is a malicious spirit that possesses a living body.

clue.text: Star men assist cast to bag award thus

indicators.note: to bag means the jumbled letters capture the award and thus words inside them
cast means the letters of assist are thrown into a new shape

parts.note: a trophy is an award
sic is Latin for thus, used to flag a quotation as written

explanation.surface: Starry men are helping a cast in their bid to win an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' turns assist into AS...ISTS, which holds TROPHY and SIC.
explanation.definitionFit: These scientists study stars and other celestial bodies.

clue.text: Old Iron Duke leaves one in ground

indicators.note: in means the one letter is placed inside what remains
leaves means the duke letter departs from the ground word

parts.note: ground food is mashed
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The Iron Duke, Wellington, departs as someone arrives on the battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Iron Duke' suggests Wellington, but Old Iron is the definition: a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: This was an old name for the golf club now called a five iron.

clue.text: One in dance (and the like) may be so

definitions.text: One in dance (and the like) may be so

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: in means the one letter goes inside the following abbreviation

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and the like
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone dancing or doing similar things may move gracefully like this.
explanation.definitionFit: A person dancing, or similar, might be graceful in the manner of ballet.

clue.text: Top down on Volkswagen

indicators.note: on means the drinking word follows the car word

parts.note: the Polo is a Volkswagen car model
to neck a drink is to down it

explanation.surface: A convertible VW with its roof lowered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top down' reads as a convertible's roof, but Top is a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sweater with a high folded collar, a garment worn on the upper body.

clue.text: Partner of entertaining prince following the king

indicators.note: entertaining means the word of holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: following means the prince comes after the king pieces

parts.note: taken as written
R, for rex, is king
Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V

explanation.surface: A consort of a prince who entertains, following the king's lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is not a link word here: it is the container, opened up by the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: One's spouse or partner is jokingly called one's better half, or this.

clue.text: Painter covers books with lines like a Turner?

indicators.note: covers means the painter letters wrap around the books letters

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
RY is short for railway, lines of track

explanation.surface: A painter covering books with lines, much as J M W Turner did.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter, but here it is something that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotary describes rotating motion, so it suits anything that spins.

clue.text: Our emperor's vexed with this creature of habit

indicators.note: vexed means the letters are agitated and jumbled

explanation.surface: An emperor upset by someone who always sticks to their routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vexed' scrambles OUR EMPEROR plus THIS; the 's is just 'is'. Habit here is a nun's robe.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a convent wears a nun's habit, so she is literally a creature in a habit.

clue.text: Figure eating puree, with recipe written down

indicators.note: eating means the number word takes the puree word inside it

parts.note: one is a figure, a number
pap is soft, pureed food
R is an abbreviation for recipe, from Latin take

explanation.surface: A cook notes down a numbered dish of puree for the recipe book.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recorded in writing exists in documented form.

clue.text: Reading or writing poorly is a barrier

parts.note: the three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so either one is R
poorly means unwell, ailing

explanation.surface: Bad literacy is an obstacle to getting on.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence of rails is a barrier along a balcony or stairway.

clue.text: See 15
Vehicle in Senegal's unoccupied border

indicators.note: unoccupied means Senegal is emptied of its middle letters

parts.note: an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A vehicle crossing the empty frontier of the African country Senegal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sled pulled over snow or ice is a vehicle on runners.

clue.text: Time of change for local ruler, content to leave timidly

parts.note: the local is one's neighbourhood pub
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

indicators.note: content to leave means the inner letters of timidly are dropped, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: Closing time at the pub, where the landlord is happy to slip off quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like happy but means contents.
explanation.definitionFit: Adolescence is when the body matures, a period of physical change.

clue.text: Awful stink over public disturbance

indicators.note: over means the stink letters are turned back to front

parts.note: BO is body odour, a stink
making a scene is causing a public disturbance

explanation.surface: A dreadful row about a bad smell becomes a public fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene can mean shockingly offensive or outrageous, as in obscene profits.

clue.text: Caring, but not up for having fun

indicators.note: not means the following word is taken out of the caring word

parts.note: supportive means caring

explanation.surface: Someone kind but not in the mood for enjoying themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Sportive means playful, describing someone frolicking for enjoyment.

clue.text: Fox to play an inspirational role?

parts.note: to play a part is to be it
a muse inspires an artist

explanation.surface: A fox is cast to inspire, perhaps as a mascot.
explanation.walkthrough: Fox is a verb, to baffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To fox someone is to puzzle or confuse them.

clue.text: Two postgraduate degrees potentially a killer

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, and an MBA, Master of Business Administration, are both postgraduate degrees
the second of the two degrees is the Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: Holding a couple of master's degrees might make someone dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a venomous African snake whose bite can be fatal.

clue.text: Hussy admits climaxing and means to be heard

indicators.note: admits means the hussy word lets the climaxing word inside it

parts.note: a strumpet is a hussy
peaking means reaching a climax

explanation.surface: A racy confession that a promiscuous woman makes herself heard.
explanation.definitionFit: This horn-shaped device amplifies the voice so it carries further.

clue.text: Asylum's official uniform for one that's flipped

parts.note: a ref, referee, is a match official
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: flipped means the example abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: eg, for example, means for one

explanation.surface: An asylum's uniformed official for someone who has gone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asylum' suggests a mental hospital, but it means sanctuary.
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum is protection or a safe place, a sanctuary for those in danger.

clue.text: Primate will do for sailor

definitions.meaning: a lemur of Madagascar with long fingers
a sailor's reply meaning yes, I will do it

explanation.surface: A monkey could stand in for a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a Madagascan lemur and a nautical assent, an acceptance of orders.
